Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
If we are given one or more factors of a polynomial, we can use these factors to continue factoring the polynomial completely. We just need to divide the polynomial by the known factors, and then continue factoring the quotient.

Content:
For example, suppose we know that [MATH: (x+2)] is a factor of [MATH: f(x) = x^4+4x^3+x^2-6x.] Then [MATH: (x+2)] divides [MATH: f(x)] with no remainder. So, to begin factoring [MATH: f(x),] we can divide it by [MATH: (x+2)] using synthetic division:

Content:
[MATH: − 2|1|4|1|− 6|0; − 2|− 4|6|0; 1|2|− 3|0|0]

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{x^4+4x^3+x^2-6x}{x+2} = x^3+2x^2-3x,]

Content:
which means that

Content:
[MATH: x^4+4x^3+x^2-6x = (x+2) (x^3+2x^2-3x).]

Content:
We can factor the cubic factor even further, and get

Content:
[MATH: (x + 2)(x^{3} + 2x^{2} − 3x)|= (x + 2)(x)(x^{2} + 2x − 3); = (x + 2)(x)(x + 3)(x − 1); = x(x + 2)(x + 3)(x − 1).]

Item 2 — Example: Factoring a Quartic Polynomial Given Two Factors

Given that [MATH: (x-1)] and [MATH: (x-3)] are factors of the polynomial [MATH: f(x)= x^4 - x^3 - 7 x^2 + x + 6,] factor [MATH: f(x)] completely.

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
To factor [MATH: f(x)] completely, we need to find its other factors.

Because [MATH: (x-1)] is a factor of [MATH: f(x),] we know that [MATH: (x-1)] divides [MATH: f(x)] with no remainder. So, to begin factoring [MATH: f(x),] we can divide it by [MATH: (x-1)] using synthetic division:

| | [MATH: x^4] | [MATH: x^3] | [MATH: x^2] | [MATH: x^1] | [MATH: x^0] |
| [MATH: \color{red}1] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: -1] | [MATH: -7] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 6] |
| | [MATH: \color{gray}\downarrow] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -7] | [MATH: -6] |
| | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -7] | [MATH: -6] | [MATH: 0] |

Therefore,

[MATH: \dfrac{x^4 - x^3 - 7 x^2 + x + 6}{x-1} = x^3-7x-6,]

which means that

[MATH: x^4 - x^3 - 7 x^2 + x + 6 = (x-1) (x^3-7x-6).]

Now, because [MATH: (x-3)] is also a factor of [MATH: f(x),] it must be a factor of the quotient [MATH: (x^3-7x-6).] So, we divide this quotient by [MATH: (x-3)] using synthetic division once more:

| | [MATH: x^3] | [MATH: x^2] | [MATH: x^1] | [MATH: x^0] |
| [MATH: \color{red}3] | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: -7] | [MATH: -6] |
| | [MATH: \color{gray}\downarrow] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 9] | [MATH: 6] |
| | [MATH: 1] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 0] |

Therefore,

[MATH: \dfrac{x^3-7x-6}{x-3} = x^2+3x +2,]

[MATH: x^4 - x^3 - 7 x^2 + x + 6 = (x-1) (x-3) (x^2+3x +2).]

We can factor the quadratic factor even further, and get
